title: Rolling SLI anchors and priority thresholds for release guardrails
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: We often push feature rollouts without a concise, machine-readable definition of SLI anchors and hard/soft priority thresholds that map to error-budget gating. This leads to inconsistent release decisions and manual reconciliation during incidents.

Proposal: Define a lightweight schema for 'SLI anchors' (primary SLI metric + sampling window + baseline/backstop), pair each anchor with a priority threshold matrix (soft warning, hard throttle, emergency rollback), and integrate these into the initiative dashboard and release gating flow. The work covers: specification, telemetry mapping, Console dashboard surface, and automation hooks for gating (canary throttle and rollout pause).

Goals:
- Reduce manual error-budget reconciliation time during deploys by 60%.
- Make release gates computable so CI/CD and the Console can surface pass/warn/fail states.
- Provide a simple UI for PMs/Eng to attach SLI anchors to initiatives and releases.
acceptance_criteria: SLI anchor JSON schema v1 published to Confluence and added to spec repo
Three priority threshold levels implemented (soft/warn, hard/throttle, critical/rollback) and documented
Telemetry mapping doc that lists exact metrics, tags, and query windows for each anchor
Console shows initiative-level SLI anchor widget with current state (pass/warn/fail) and recent trend sparkline
Automation prototype: canary rollout pauses when hard threshold breached in the last 5m window
Playbook entry for oncall describing steps for manual override and post-mortem reconciliation
implementation_notes: Start with 3 pilot initiatives (Console routing, Embeddings ingestion, and Dedicated autoscaler) to validate schema
Telemetry owners: assign metric owners per pilot in ENG and Observability
Use existing KV-cache SLI as reference for sampling windows and bucketing logic
Integrate with the Initiative Tracker API so PMs can attach anchors during roadmap planning
Prototype gating via a lightweight webhook that receives pass/warn/fail and signals rollout controller
